{
  "subtype": "exploratory_data_analysis",
  "focus_variable": "resolution_time",
  "per_column": [
    {
      "name": "infrastructure_domain",
      "role": "predictor",
      "is_predictor": true,
      "is_interpretable_segmentation": true,
      "rationale": "Interpretable, well-separated categories (email, database, VPN, network) derived from ticket content. Resolution time can be meaningfully compared across these domains, complementing the given 'category' column with a technical-domain lens."
    },
    {
      "name": "problem_severity",
      "role": "predictor",
      "is_predictor": true,
      "is_interpretable_segmentation": true,
      "rationale": "Severity levels (outage_system_wide, partial_access, performance_degraded) form an ordered, interpretable scale that plausibly associates with resolution_time and supports segmentation."
    },
    {
      "name": "resolution_completion_status",
      "role": "restatement",
      "is_predictor": false,
      "is_interpretable_segmentation": false,
      "rationale": "A boolean of whether the ticket was resolved/closed. This is downstream of and near-tautological with resolution_time (unresolved tickets have no/ongoing resolution time); it restates the focus rather than offering an external associational variable."
    },
    {
      "name": "incident_scope",
      "role": "predictor",
      "is_predictor": true,
      "is_interpretable_segmentation": true,
      "rationale": "Scope categories (system_wide, single_user, department_scoped) are interpretable and well-separated, and blast radius plausibly relates to how long resolution takes. Note partial overlap with problem_severity, but still a distinct segmentation axis."
    },
    {
      "name": "authentication_access_failure",
      "role": "predictor",
      "is_predictor": true,
      "is_interpretable_segmentation": true,
      "rationale": "A clear binary flag with reasonable class balance (76/424) marking auth/access issues; a plausible, interpretable dimension to compare resolution times against."
    },
    {
      "name": "technician_assignment_continuity",
      "role": "predictor",
      "is_predictor": true,
      "is_interpretable_segmentation": true,
      "rationale": "Whether the ticket stayed with one technician vs. was reassigned; balanced binary (216/284) and process-oriented, directly plausible as a driver of resolution time and interpretable for a human explorer."
    }
  ],
  "n_predictors": 5,
  "relationship_informativeness": 0.72,
  "rationale": "Five of six columns are external, interpretable, well-separated segmentations (domain, severity, scope, auth flag, assignment continuity) that a human can group on and compare against resolution_time, going beyond the given category/priority/group. Several overlap conceptually (severity vs. scope vs. auth), slightly reducing distinctiveness. The main failure is resolution_completion_status, which is essentially a restatement of the focus (resolution outcome) and offers no independent relationship. Overall a strong EDA-oriented set with one tautological inclusion."
}
